title: Why Use JSON Schema from DuckDB?
description: [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/) is the de facto contract language for JSON payloads — a declarative way to say what a document must look like. This extension makes those contracts *executable* from inside DuckDB, so a data-quality gate, an ETL contract check, or a default-value fill-in can live in SQL instead of a Pydantic / ajv / jsonschema sidecar. It is built on the [pboettch/json-schema-validator](https://github.com/pboettch/json-schema-validator) C++ library, whose primary target is [JSON Schema draft-07](https://json-schema.org/draft-07/json-schema-release-notes).

sections.title: JSON Schema as an in-SQL contract
sections.description: The idea is to treat a schema as a contract that a column of JSON must satisfy, and to enforce that contract where the data already lives. Validation answers a single question — does this value conform? — which makes it a `BOOLEAN` predicate that drops straight into `WHERE`, `CASE`, and aggregate `FILTER` clauses. Beyond pure validation, the schema's declared `default` values can also be projected onto incomplete documents to bring them into conformance.

bulletPoints.label: Draft-07 is the target
bulletPoints.description: The underlying validator primarily targets [draft-07](https://json-schema.org/draft-07/json-schema-release-notes). The `$schema` keyword in your document is honored where the validator supports it; for newer drafts ([2019-09](https://json-schema.org/specification-links#2019-09), [2020-12](https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema)), test the specific keywords you use rather than assuming full coverage.

bulletPoints.label: What the validator covers
bulletPoints.description: Coverage matches what draft-07 specifies: type checks (`string`, `number`, `integer`, `boolean`, `array`, `object`, `null`), `required`, `properties`, numeric `minimum` / `maximum` / `multipleOf`, string `minLength` / `maxLength` / `pattern` / `format`, array `minItems` / `maxItems` / `uniqueItems`, and the `default` keyword that powers default-value enrichment.

bulletPoints.label: Schema and data are both JSON
bulletPoints.description: Both the schema and the value under test are passed as DuckDB [`JSON`](https://duckdb.org/docs/data/json/overview) values — a column, a struct literal, or a string cast with `::JSON`. There's no preregistration step, no `ATTACH`, no secret type, and no network: validation runs locally against the in-query schema string.

bulletPoints.label: Default-value enrichment, not just validation
bulletPoints.description: The non-obvious capability: turn the schema's declared `default` values into actual data. One function computes the [JSON Patch (RFC 6902)](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6902) diff of `add` operations (useful for an audit log); another applies them inline — taking an incomplete payload to a fully populated record in one expression, with no `COALESCE` cascade.

sections.title: What to know before relying on it
sections.description: The extension is small and focused; it doesn't try to be every JSON-Schema validator out there. Knowing its boundaries keeps it in the role it's good at — a coarse SQL-side gate — rather than where a richer tool belongs.

bulletPoints.label: Boolean result, not an error report
bulletPoints.description: Validation returns `TRUE` / `FALSE`, not a structured list of which keywords or paths failed. For per-keyword diagnostics, validate at the application layer with [ajv](https://ajv.js.org/), [Pydantic](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/json_schema/), or [jsonschema](https://python-jsonschema.readthedocs.io/), and use this extension as the coarse SQL gate at ingest, in CI, or in an audit.

bulletPoints.label: No cross-file `$ref` resolution
bulletPoints.description: Each call takes a single `JSON` schema value — there is no filesystem or HTTP `$ref` resolver. Inline any `$ref` targets into the same schema document before validating.

bulletPoints.label: Prefer typed columns where you can
bulletPoints.description: If the data has a fixed shape, modeling it as proper DuckDB columns plus [`CHECK` constraints](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/constraints) is cheaper, clearer, and gives better error messages. JSON Schema validation is for the genuinely-JSON case where the shape is contract-defined but the storage stays opaque.

bulletPoints.label: Per-row cost scales with schema complexity
bulletPoints.description: Deeply-nested schemas with many keywords run the full validator on every row. For very large tables, validate once on ingest into a staging table rather than re-running the check on every read.
